newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm trade surplus $1.061 billion in May.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm trade surplus $1.061 billion in May.

text.p: The U.S. trade surplus in agricultural commodities was $1.061 billion in May, down from $1.440 billion in April, the Commerce Department said Friday.
In its monthly trade report, Commerce pegged farm exports at $4.248 billion in May, compared with $4.519 in April. Imports rose to $3.187 billion in May, from $3.079 billion the preceding month.

Exports of major U.S. crops fell in May. Soybean shipments totalled $374 million, down $140 million, while wheat was off $102 million to total $228 million. Corn sales totalled $416 million, compared with $503 million in April and cotton totalled $232 million, a $36 million drop.
Raw tobacco nearly doubled, reaching $226 million from April's $133 million.

Imports of coffee, flour and rice were up modestly. Sugar imports totalled $97 million, compared with $55 million the preceding month. Shipments of fruits and vegetables, at $692 million, were down $48 million.
